definition: persistently demanding to the point of annoyance
memoryTip: Im-PORTUNE: keep porting the same ask until it’s annoying.
correctPassage: Importunate callers continued to press the office for an earlier hearing long after the deadline had passed.
wrongPassages: The importunate intern waited quietly and never repeated a request once it had been declined.
A single courteous note was enough to make her approach seem importunate to the entire board.
His importunate withdrawal from the debate left colleagues free of any further appeals.

definition: skill in performing tasks, especially with the hands
memoryTip: Dexterous hands — think “Dexter” building gadgets with skill.
correctPassage: Assembling the microcircuit demanded exceptional manual dexterity and steady focus.
wrongPassages: Judges praised his dexterity after he fumbled the tools and broke two samples.
The technician’s dexterity showed most clearly in how slowly and awkwardly she handled the instruments.
They measured the surgeon’s dexterity by how often instruments slipped from her grip.

memoryTip: Ir-respective: without respect to X — regardless of it.
correctPassage: The scholarship is awarded on academic merit, irrespective of family income.
wrongPassages: Funding decisions were made irrespective of need, meaning only the wealthiest applicants were considered.
The policy applies irrespective of major only when the major is engineering.
She chose the laboratory assignment irrespective of her interest, carefully matching every preference.

definition: excessive pride in appearance or achievements
memoryTip: Vain about looks or status — vanity is that excessive pride.
correctPassage: Critics argued that the renovation was motivated more by vanity than by any genuine public need.
wrongPassages: Her vanity showed when she credited the whole team and stepped out of the commemorative photo.
He treated vanity as pure selflessness, quietly declining every award offered to him.
The plain cabin, built without mirrors or display, was widely admired as a monument to vanity.

memoryTip: Can’t see through it — glass that blocks light, or prose that blocks meaning.
correctPassage: The selection process remained opaque to anyone outside the small review committee.
wrongPassages: The glass partition was so opaque that every desk in the office was clearly visible from the hall.
Her opaque summary listed each step in plain language a newcomer could follow at once.
Editors praised the report as opaque because its logic was open and easy to check.
